title: Key-Alternating Ciphers with Minimal Key Scheduling
summary: Provable results exist for key-alternating ciphers using public permutations and simple constants, but whether they can guide efficient lightweight designs with minimal key scheduling remains open.

formal_statement.body: For key-alternating block-cipher constructions based on public permutations and simple constants, determine whether the provable results for this setting can guide alternative block-cipher designs with minimal key-scheduling algorithms, including a variant of AES in which round keys are replaced by simple constants, and whether such an approach can produce efficient lightweight designs.

scope.domain: Design of key-alternating block ciphers using public permutations, simple constants, and minimal key scheduling.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the provable results can guide minimal-key-schedule designs, including the proposed AES variant, and produce efficient lightweight block ciphers.

citations.label: Key-Alternating Ciphers in a Provable Setting: Encryption Using a Small Number of Public Permutations - (Extended Abstract)

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents applying its provable results to alternative block-cipher designs with minimal key scheduling as an open problem. It offers replacing AES round keys with simple constants as a possible route toward efficient lightweight designs.
